answer: Tie an agent's standing to a refundable bond plus reputation earned only through time-stamped, peer-attested work. Trust accrues slowly, the way a river carves a canyon, with no shortcut. A sudden gale of fresh identities buys nothing: each fake needs its own locked bond and months of verifiable history, so a sybil fleet costs the attacker roughly as much as honest participation. The economics, not mere detection, make the attack unprofitable.
